stemMd: Which statement about benzene is correct?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It is a saturated open-chain hydrocarbon.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Every carbon is bonded to four hydrogen atoms.

options.label: E
options.textMd: Its ring has a delocalized pi-electron system.

explanationMd: Benzene is a six-carbon ring with a delocalized pi system distributed around the ring. It is not adequately represented as three isolated double bonds with ordinary alkene behaviour. The molecular formula C₆H₆ and ring structure distinguish it from an alkane.

distractorRationale.a: Benzene is a cyclic aromatic compound.
distractorRationale.b: Its bonding is covalent with delocalized pi electrons.
distractorRationale.c: That formula belongs to a saturated acyclic six-carbon hydrocarbon.
distractorRationale.d: Each benzene carbon is bonded to only one hydrogen.
